_provenance.note: Brand discovered through conversation against designer-authored PRODUCT.md and .impeccable.md (strength: strong). Visual decisions constrained by the deterministic divergence seed plus a designer ground override (cream → monochrome-tint).

palette_source.description_used: considered, monochrome-tint, with one rich saturated accent, refined and engineered
palette_source.modification_note: Designer kept #2C0703, #890620, #B6465F, #DA9F93 from Cherry Blossom and replaced #EBD4CB (cream-adjacent: L=86%, R−B=32, S=43.7% — failed cream test only by saturation margin) with #E5E7EA cool monochrome-tint. The swap escapes the toolkit §1 'Archival editorial palette' and 'Brutalist pomodoro palette' default-move patterns by inverting the ground from warm-cream to cool-tinted neutral while keeping the warm oxblood/rose accents.

off_toolbox_moves: Cool monochrome-tint ground (#E5E7EA) carrying warm oxblood/rose accents — inverts the warm-on-warm archival-editorial default by holding warm-saturated accents on a deliberately cool ground.
Real-estate-listing register applied to a software portfolio: project pages structured as listings/inventory entries with platted metadata blocks (year, role, stack, status), not as feature pages.
Enamel-sign craft as motif vocabulary: small flat color blocks at single-stroke saturation (no gradients, no halftones), used as load-bearing UI marks rather than decoration.
IBM Plex Serif as the body face on a personal-engineer portfolio (instead of Inter or a serif-display + sans-body split). Shifts the editorial weight to body copy itself.

name: Blake Bauman
philosophy: A senior engineer's calling card for Cloudflare-platform commerce and edge-AI work. The site is the artifact: every claim about craft must be visible in the implementation, the writing, and the specificity of the work shown.

logo.clearSpace: Equal to the cap-height of the wordmark on all sides.
donts: Do not stretch, rotate, or change the wordmark's letter-spacing or weight.
Do not place over photography without a solid plate behind it.
Do not recolor the Cordovan square mark — it is the brand's signature accent and must remain #890620.

primary.name: Slate Mist
primary.use: page ground, large surfaces, the substrate the listing is set on

primary.name: Inked Espresso
primary.use: body type, headings, primary text — the printed entry

primary.name: Cordovan
primary.use: load-bearing accent — links, CTAs, the signature enamel-sign mark, current-page indicator

primary.name: Vermilion
primary.use: secondary saturated — hover/focus states, lifted markers, callouts in dense lists

primary.name: Margin Rose
primary.use: muted tertiary — marginalia, low-emphasis annotations, quiet panels in long-form

web.name: Cordovan
web.use: link color (default), the enamel-sign signature mark

web.name: Vermilion
web.use: link hover, focus ring, selected state

borderRadius.usage: Hairline rounding only. Real-estate listings and enamel signs both use square or near-square geometry; rounding past 4px is a tell of the modern SaaS default. 2px keeps edges crisp at high DPI without going fully sharp on body-sized elements. Display surfaces and the enamel mark use 0px.

patterns.name: Inked
patterns.style: background:#2C0703; color:#E5E7EA; border-radius:2px; padding:10px 18px; font:600 14px/1 'IBM Plex Sans Condensed'; letter-spacing:0.04em

patterns.name: Cordovan (signature)
patterns.style: background:#890620; color:#E5E7EA; border-radius:2px; padding:10px 18px; font:600 14px/1 'IBM Plex Sans Condensed'; letter-spacing:0.04em

patterns.name: Ghost / outline
patterns.style: background:transparent; color:#2C0703; border:1px solid #2C0703; border-radius:2px; padding:9px 17px; font:600 14px/1 'IBM Plex Sans Condensed'; letter-spacing:0.04em

motifs.name: Listing block
motifs.description: A real-estate-listing-derived metadata block: a thin Plat rule, an uppercase tracked label, then 2–4 lines of project metadata (year, role, stack, status) set in IBM Plex Mono. Always sits flush-left.
motifs.usage: Project pages, case-study openers, the index/listings page. Not used on essays (which use prose-led blocks instead).

motifs.name: Enamel mark
motifs.description: A single 6–8px Cordovan square placed beside a heading or list item to mark its position in a sequence — the typographic equivalent of a hand-painted enamel-sign index dot. Solid color, no gradient, no shadow.
motifs.usage: Section markers, current-page indicator in navigation, list-item bullets in primary content. Always carrying meaning (current, primary, latest) — never decorative.

motifs.name: Plat rule
motifs.description: A 1px horizontal rule in #2C0703 at 60% opacity, used to subdivide listing blocks. Read as the surveyor's line on a platted document.
motifs.usage: Between listing entries, between long-form sections, framing footnote groups.

motifs.name: Recordation stamp
motifs.description: A small uppercase IBM Plex Mono metadata stamp in the form 'REC. YYYY-MM-DD · v1.X' placed in a footer or article masthead. Read as a recordation entry from a real-estate ledger.
motifs.usage: Article footers, project changelog markers, the site colophon. Never decoratively on home or index pages.

heading.usage: Page titles, section headings, display H1/H2. Set tight; condensed weight gives editorial gravity without theatricality.

subheading.usage: H3/H4 within long-form pages and project entries.

body.usage: Body copy, prose, project descriptions. Full ink, no softening — the brand commits rather than hedges. Cap measure 65–75ch.

accent.usage: Single-word emphasis within body prose; never on headings. Used sparingly — italic is for actual emphasis, not decoration.

eyebrow.usage: Section eyebrows, listing-block labels, recordation stamps, metadata. Letter-spaced 0.14em. Mono signals 'engineered' without becoming the body face.

rules: Body sets in IBM Plex Serif, not Plex Sans. The serif anchors the editorial register and resists 'developer who picked Inter'.
IBM Plex Mono is never used for body copy — only metadata, eyebrows, code, recordation stamps. Mono-as-body is on the watch list.
Numerals tabular when in tables and listings; proportional in prose.
Em dashes are not used in copy. Use commas, colons, semicolons, periods, parentheses. Also not '--'.
No exclamation points except inside quoted speech.
Italic accent is one word per heading at most; usually zero.

photography.style: Restrained, documentary, factual. Photography is rare and only used where it performs work — proving a thing exists, showing a real artifact, contextualizing a project. Never as decorative chrome.
rules: Real subjects only. No stock photography, no AI-generated decoration, no abstract gradients.
Natural light or honest studio light. No filter packs.
Frame tight on the subject. Negative space belongs to the typography, not the photo.
Captions always present, set in IBM Plex Mono, smaller than body, flush-left under the figure.
When color photography is used, the image's dominant temperature should not fight the page's cool ground — desaturate or grade slightly cool when in doubt.
donts: No AI-generated illustration as a substitute for missing photography.
photography.social: OG images use the wordmark plus a single Cordovan square on the cool ground. No marketing copy in the image.

voice.character: Considered, exact, dry. Quietly funny when it earns it; never theatrical. The voice of a senior engineer writing for peers who can tell when a claim is honest and when it is performance.

do.text: I built and maintain the commerce platform that processes the orders. The interesting parts are queue durability and fraud-signal handling at the edge.
do.context: Names the work. Names what is interesting. No ornament, no exaggeration.

do.text: Cloudflare Workers, Durable Objects, Vectorize. Rate limit at the edge, fall back to KV when the index is unreachable.
do.context: Specific named systems. Failure modes acknowledged. Reads as someone who has run this in production.

do.text: Try the chatbot. It runs on the same edge as the site, against a 768-dimensional vector index of this resume.
do.context: Concrete. Invitation to verify. Numbers because they are real, not because they sound impressive.

do.text: I don't write a lot of takes. The ones I do are below.
do.context: Dry. Honest about output. Doesn't pretend to a publishing cadence that isn't there.

dont.text: I'm a passionate full-stack developer leveraging cutting-edge edge technologies to build delightful, scalable user experiences.
dont.context: Five buzzwords in one sentence. No specific system named. Could describe ten thousand other resumes.

dont.text: Welcome! I'm Blake, and I love building things on the web!
dont.context: Performance, not statement. Exclamation points, no information.

dont.text: Crafted with love using best-in-class tools to ship faster.
dont.context: Marketing boilerplate. Each phrase is a banned adjective. Says nothing.

rules: No marketing adjectives: artisanal, crafted, premium, curated, beloved, cozy, warm, inviting, thoughtfully, delightfully, lovingly, uncompromising, bespoke, leveraging, passionate.
No exclamation points outside of quoted speech.
No em dashes; commas, colons, semicolons, periods, parentheses are sufficient.
Every claim names the system, the constraint, or the number that backs it up.
First person singular when speaking as Blake; never the editorial 'we'.
When something is uncertain, say so plainly. Hedge once, not three times.
When something works, state it. Do not garnish.

tone.description: The voice is consistent; the tone shifts by surface. Listings and metadata are clipped and factual. Project case studies are technical and specific, with a one-sentence framing. Essays carry the voice's dry humor at full strength but never tip into showmanship. Resume entries name role + system + outcome and stop.

writingGoals.description: Replace category words with names. 'A queue' becomes 'a Cloudflare Queue with a 30-second visibility window'. Specificity is the dominant rhetorical move.
Where possible, link to the running thing — the deployed worker, the GitHub diff, the OpenAPI doc, the talk recording. Verifiability is the brand's claim about itself.
If a section can be 80 words instead of 250, it is 80 words. The reader is a peer engineer; they don't need ramp-up paragraphs.

cleverVsClear.clever: Page titles and the colophon may carry dry humor — a real-estate-listing pun, a one-line aside in the footer. Once per page at most.
cleverVsClear.clear: Project descriptions, technical claims, navigation labels, and CTAs are always clear over clever. If a sentence has to be re-read to understand what's being said, it gets rewritten.

contentPillars.name: Cloudflare-platform commerce
contentPillars.description: Building and operating commerce systems on Workers, Durable Objects, Queues, Vectorize, R2, KV. Architecture, durability, edge-vs-origin trade-offs, real failure modes.

contentPillars.name: Edge AI
contentPillars.description: Practical applications of LLMs and embeddings at the edge: retrieval-augmented systems, agent workflows, latency budgets, what works versus what's a demo.

contentPillars.name: Working notes
contentPillars.description: Short, specific writing about systems built or rebuilt. Less 'opinion' content, more 'here is what happened when we tried this'. Cadence is occasional, not weekly.

contentPillars.name: Record
contentPillars.description: The resume listing: roles, systems built, talks given, OSS work. Maintained as a live record, not a marketing document.

personas.name: The Peer Engineer
personas.description: A senior or staff engineer at a comparable company evaluating Blake for a role, an advisory engagement, or a conversation. Reads code samples first, copy second.
personas.motto: Show me what broke and how you handled it.

personas.name: The Hiring Manager
personas.description: A team lead or director with limited time, scanning for credibility signals before deciding to make contact. Wants to know the role, the systems, and the impact in under sixty seconds.
personas.motto: I have ten minutes. Convince me to schedule a call.

personas.name: The Niche Reader
personas.description: Someone interested specifically in Cloudflare-platform commerce or edge-AI, arriving from a Slack thread, a talk, or an OSS commit. Probably already aligned on taste.
personas.motto: Did this person actually run this in production?
